title: 537. Emperors of Rome: Claudius, Paranoia and Poison (Part 4)

sentences.en: When the conspirators who were lurking in wait for Caligula moved everyone else along, on the grounds that the emperor wished to be alone,
sentences.zh: 正当潜伏起来等待卡利古拉的刺客们以皇帝想要独处为由，把其他所有人都支开时，

sentences.en: Claudius retreated to a wing of the palace known as the Hermaeum.
sentences.zh: 克劳迪乌斯退到了皇宫中一个被称为赫尔梅乌姆的侧翼。

sentences.en: Not long afterwards, alarmed by their distant shouts of
sentences.zh: 不久之后，他被远处传来的喊声惊动，

sentences.en: MURDER, crept away to a nearby balcony, where he hid himself behind the curtains hanging in front of the door.
sentences.zh: 那喊声是“谋杀”，他悄悄溜到了附近的一个阳台上，把自己藏在门前悬挂的窗帘后面。

sentences.en: There he cowered.
sentences.zh: 他在那里畏缩着。

sentences.en: And as he did so, a soldier who happened to be wandering past noticed his feet and dragged him out, intending to ask him who he was.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一个恰巧路过的士兵注意到了他的双脚，把他拖了出来，打算盘问他的身份。

sentences.en: But then, as he sank to his knees in terror, recognised him and hailed him as Emperor.
sentences.zh: 但随后，当他惊恐得瘫软在地时，那士兵认出了他，并高呼他为皇帝。

sentences.en: The soldier then led him away to where the other Praetorians were all milling around, uncertain what to do.
sentences.zh: 接着，士兵把他带到了其他近卫军聚集、不知所措的地方。

sentences.en: The soldiers put him in a litter, and because his own attendants had run away, took it in turns to carry the unhappy and fearful man on their shoulders to their camp,
sentences.zh: 士兵们把他塞进了一辆轿子里，由于他自己的随从都跑光了，他们便轮流把这个既痛苦又恐惧的男人抬到了他们的军营，

sentences.en: and all the crowds they passed on the way pitied him, on the assumption that he was an innocent being bundled off to execution.
sentences.zh: 一路上他们经过的群众都对他心生怜悯，以为他是一个被五花大绑去处决的无辜之人。

sentences.en: Received within the ramparts, he spent the night under the protection of the Praetorians, but in a mood of relief rather than of any great expectation.
sentences.zh: 进入营垒后，他在近卫军的保护下过了一夜，但与其说是充满巨大期望，不如说是松了一口气。

sentences.en: But as the next day passed, so large crowds of people gathered outside the Praetorian camp, agitating for a single man to be given rule, and calling for Claudius by name.
sentences.zh: 但随着第二天过去，大批民众聚集在近卫军军营外，煽动由一人统治，并高呼克劳迪乌斯的名字。

sentences.en: These chants prompted him to allow an armed assembly of the Praetorians to swear allegiance to him, and to promise each one of them 15,000 sesterces,
sentences.zh: 这些呼喊声促使他允许武装的近卫军向他效忠，并承诺向他们每人支付1.5万塞斯特斯，

sentences.en: thereby becoming the first of the Caesars to win the loyalty of the military by paying them a bribe.
sentences.zh: 从而成为凯撒中第一个通过行贿赢得军队忠诚的人。

sentences.en: So that last sentence, I'm not sure whether that's really true, but that's Suetonius in his life of Claudius,
sentences.zh: 所以最后这句话，我不知道是不是真的，但这是苏维托尼乌斯在他的《克劳迪乌斯传》中写的，

sentences.en: as translated in the new Penguin Classics edition by our very own Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 正如我们自己的汤姆·霍兰在企鹅经典的新版本中所翻译的那样。

sentences.en: And Tom there, Suetonius, is taking the story forwards from where we left it last time.
sentences.zh: 而汤姆和苏维托尼乌斯，正在把故事从我们上次结束的地方推进下去。

sentences.en: We left it on a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 我们把它停在一个悬念上。

sentences.en: The Emperor Caligula, mad or not, definitely a populist, has been assassinated by Cassius Caerea and the Praetorian Guard.
sentences.zh: 皇帝卡利古拉，不管疯不疯，绝对是个民粹主义者，已经被卡修斯·凯里亚和近卫军刺杀身亡。

sentences.en: And the question is, is Rome going to turn back the clock 60 years to the time of the Republic and all the chaos at the end of the Republic,
sentences.zh: 问题是，罗马是要把时钟拨回60年前的共和国时期以及共和国末期的所有混乱，

sentences.en: or is it going to continue with the family of Augustus, known as the Caesars?
sentences.zh: 还是要继续由奥古斯都的家族——也就是被称为凯撒的人统治？

sentences.en: So take us forward.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it's the pressing question.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，这是一个紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Is there an eligible Caesar to hand?
sentences.zh: 手头有没有合适的凯撒人选？

sentences.en: Or, as you were implying, might it be time to turn the clock back, to go back to the Republican system of government?
sentences.zh: 或者，正如你刚才所暗示的，也许是时候把时钟拨回去，回到共和制的政府体制了？

sentences.en: And what makes that question even more pressing is the fact that, as we've been saying throughout this series, the autocracy of the Caesars is not formally a hereditary monarchy.
sentences.zh: 让这个问题变得更加紧迫的是这样一个事实：正如我们在整个系列中所说的那样，凯撒的独裁统治形式上并不是世袭君主制。

sentences.en: In fact, formally, it's not a monarchy at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，形式上它根本不是君主制。

sentences.en: And so there are no rules governing the succession.
sentences.zh: 因此，没有任何规章制度来规范继承权。

sentences.en: That said, it has come to be accepted that the emperor should be a Caesar.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，人们已经普遍接受皇帝应该是一个凯撒。

sentences.en: So that means an heir, either by adoption, as was the case with Tiberius, or by bloodline, as was the case with Caligula, of the deified Augustus,
sentences.zh: 这意味着他是神圣奥古斯都的继承人，要么是通过收养（如提比略），要么是通过血脉（如卡利古拉），

sentences.en: the first of the emperors and who is now a god.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都是第一位皇帝，现在已经是一位神了。

sentences.en: So the question then is, what are the options?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，有哪些选择？

sentences.en: Who is there on hand?
sentences.zh: 手头都有谁？

sentences.en: And I suppose the obvious question, which we didn't touch on in our episode on Caligula,
sentences.zh: 我想最显而易见的问题是，我们在关于卡利古拉的那期节目中没有涉及到的，

sentences.en: is, has he left any children?
sentences.zh: 那就是，他留下什么孩子了吗？

sentences.en: And although he's only 28 when he gets murdered,
sentences.zh: 尽管他被谋杀时年仅28岁，

sentences.en: he hasn't stinted when it comes to having wives.
sentences.zh: 但在娶妻方面他可一点也没含糊。

sentences.en: I mean, he's burned through a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他换过很多妻子。

sentences.en: And his last wife is the one that actually seems to have been his great love.
sentences.zh: 他的最后一个妻子似乎确实是他此生真爱。

sentences.en: And she's a woman called Melonia Cezonia.
sentences.zh: 那是一个叫梅洛尼亚·切索尼亚的女人。

sentences.en: And she isn't particularly young.
sentences.zh: 她并不是特别年轻。

sentences.en: She's not particularly attractive.
sentences.zh: 她也算不上特别迷人。

sentences.en: But she does seem to have appealed to something very deep in Caligula.
sentences.zh: 但她似乎确实触动了卡利古拉内心深处的一些东西。

sentences.en: I mean, he really knows.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他真的很清楚。

sentences.en: Well, actually, I think we can have a fairly good idea what it is.
sentences.zh: 好吧，其实，我想我们可以大致猜到是什么。

sentences.en: They both seem to have certainly had a taste for dressing up.
sentences.zh: 他们俩似乎都对变装有着特殊的爱好。

sentences.en: Like Lucy Worsley.
sentences.zh: 就像露西·沃斯利一样。

sentences.en: A bit like, well, to a degree.
sentences.zh: 有点像，嗯，在某种程度上。

sentences.en: So when he goes riding off to see soldiers or whatever, he dresses her up in a military outfit as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他骑马去见士兵或做其他事情时，他也会给她穿上军装。

sentences.en: So she clearly enjoys that.
sentences.zh: 所以她显然很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: But he also gets her to pose nude for friends.
sentences.zh: 但他也让在朋友面前摆出裸体姿势。

sentences.en: So to that extent, she's not like Lucy Worsley.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，她不像露西·沃斯利。

sentences.en: But she's clearly, she's a fun girl.
sentences.zh: 但她显然是个有趣的女孩。

sentences.en: Well, OK, she gels well with Caligula's inimitable madcap sense of humour.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，她和卡利古拉那独一无二、异想天开的幽默感十分合拍。

sentences.en: I think she's a zany funster.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她是个滑稽有趣的活宝。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she has given him one child.
sentences.zh: 她给他生了一个孩子。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, for fans of the bloodline of Caligula, that child is a daughter.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，对于卡利古拉血脉的粉丝来说，那个孩子是个女儿。

sentences.en: And Caligula has named her after his beloved sister who died and whom he deified in his grief.
sentences.zh: 卡利古拉用他那死去的、他在悲痛中将其神化的挚爱姐姐的名字给她命名。

sentences.en: So he calls her Julia Drusilla.
sentences.zh: 所以他叫她茱莉亚·德鲁西拉。

sentences.en: And she's a lovely, sweet-natured girl, isn't she, by all accounts?
sentences.zh: 根据各方说法，她是个可爱、天性甜美的女孩，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this, again, I think is one of the, I mean, very funny bit from Suetonius.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是，我认为，苏维托尼乌斯非常有趣的一个片段。

sentences.en: So this is Caligula talking about Drusilla.
sentences.zh: 这是卡利古拉在谈论德鲁西拉。

sentences.en: There existed no surer evidence that she was indeed his child, he believed, than her temper, which was so violent, whenever she played with other little children,
sentences.zh: 他认为，没有任何确凿的证据比她的脾气更能证明她确实是他的骨肉，每当她和其他小孩子玩耍时，她的脾气是如此暴躁，

sentences.en: she would scratch at their faces and jab at their eyes with her fingers.
sentences.zh: 她会用手指去抓他们的脸，去戳他们的眼睛。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 太美妙了。

sentences.en: So daddy watches on.
sentences.zh: 所以爸爸就在一旁看着。

sentences.en: Oh, chip off the old block.
sentences.zh: 哦，有其父必有其子。

sentences.en: So what happens to them?
sentences.zh: 那么他们的结局如何？

sentences.en: Well, according to Suetonius, they get murdered along with Caligula.
sentences.zh: 好吧，根据苏维托尼乌斯的说法，他们和卡利古拉一起被谋杀了。

sentences.en: He says that they've been accompanying him when they run into the Praetorians.
sentences.zh: 他说，当他们撞上近卫军时，正陪着卡利古拉。

sentences.en: But Josephus, the great Judean historian who has very precise information about what happens, he reports that they weren't with him.
sentences.zh: 但伟大的犹太历史学家约瑟夫斯对发生的事情有着非常精确的信息，他报道说他们并不和他在一起。

sentences.en: But when the news came that he'd been murdered, they come and seek out the body of their husband stroke father.
sentences.zh: 但当卡利古拉被谋杀的消息传来时，他们赶来寻找他们身为丈夫兼父亲的尸体。

sentences.en: And they find him and they kind of lie prostrated with grief, mourning him.
sentences.zh: 当他们找到他时，悲痛欲绝地俯卧哀悼着他。

sentences.en: And this is where they are found by a Praetorian who has been sent to dispatch them.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，他们被一个奉命去处决他们的近卫军士兵发现了。

sentences.en: And Cezonia looks up at the soldier and she's, you know, sobbing.
sentences.zh: 切索尼亚抬头看着那个士兵，你知道的，她在啜泣。

sentences.en: And she says, finish the last act of the drama.
sentences.zh: 她说，演完这出戏的最后一幕吧。

sentences.en: So again, this idea that everyone in the House of Caesar is an actor on a stage.
sentences.zh: 所以，这再次体现了这种观点：凯撒家族的每个人都是舞台上的演员。

sentences.en: And the Praetorian duly does as he's told.
sentences.zh: 而近卫军也照着命令行事了。

sentences.en: He slits Cezonia's throat and he picks up little Drusilla and he smashes out her brains
sentences.zh: 他割断了切索尼亚的喉咙，抱起小德鲁西拉，把她的脑袋砸碎

sentences.en: on the side of a wall.
sentences.zh: 在墙壁上。

sentences.en: So that's the end of them.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的结局。

sentences.en: So they have gone.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就这样离去了。

sentences.en: And there are no male descendants of Augustus at all, full stop.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都的男性后代已经一个不剩了。

sentences.en: And there's no male candidate with the blood of Augustus in their veins to succeed Caligula.
sentences.zh: 也没有任何流着奥古斯都血液的男性候选人能够继承卡利古拉。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that there are many in the Senate who do think, well, this might be the time to bring back the Republic to kind of wake up from this terrible nightmare
sentences.zh: 因此，参议院里有许多人认为，这或许是恢复共和国的时机，好从我们一直经历的这场可怕噩梦中醒来，这也就不足为奇了

sentences.en: that we've been living through.
sentences.zh: 我们一直生活在其中。

sentences.en: And so that evening, you know, the soldiers come, the guards come and they say to the consuls who've taken control of the city now that Caligula's gone and they say, what's
sentences.zh: 所以在那个傍晚，你知道的，士兵们、卫兵们来了，他们对那些在卡利古拉死后控制了城市的执政官说，

sentences.en: the watchword?
sentences.zh: 口令是什么？

sentences.en: And they say, liberty.
sentences.zh: 他们回答说，自由。

sentences.en: Oh, so it's all very noble and upstanding.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以这一切都显得非常崇高和正派。

sentences.en: And the next day they have a kind of very grandiose, florid debate on the need to restore the
sentences.zh: 第二天，他们就恢复共和国的必要性展开了一场非常宏大、辞藻华丽的辩论。

sentences.en: Republic.
sentences.zh: 共和国。

sentences.en: Words like liberty and various other abstractions are bandied around with great abandon.
sentences.zh: 诸如自由之类的词汇以及其他各种抽象概念被大加挥霍。

sentences.en: But while they are having this debate, they are forgetting the fact that there are other players in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 但当他们进行这场辩论时，他们忘记了这场危机中还有其他参与者。

sentences.en: One group of which, of course, is the Praetorians.
sentences.zh: 其中一个群体，当然就是近卫军。

sentences.en: It's the imperial guard who, some of whom had been prompted to murder Caligula, but who absolutely do not want to see the overthrow of the monarchy because they depend on it for
sentences.zh: 正是这支御林军，其中一些人曾促成了对卡利古拉的谋杀，但他们绝对不愿意看到君主制的覆灭，因为他们依靠君主制来维持

sentences.en: their status and their income.
sentences.zh: 他们的地位和收入。

sentences.en: So obviously they don't want to repubulate.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，他们不想恢复共和国。

sentences.en: There'd be no role for them.
sentences.zh: 那样就不会有他们的容身之地了。

sentences.en: And the other kind of player in the drama, of course, is the people, the mass of the Roman people who likewise mourn Caligula.
sentences.zh: 当然，这场戏中的另一类参与者，就是民众，广大罗马民众同样在哀悼卡利古拉。

sentences.en: They're very upset that he's gone and they too want a Caesar because it is Caesar who keeps them fed above all.
sentences.zh: 他对他的离去感到非常难过，他们也想要一个凯撒，因为正是凯撒保证了他们的温饱。

sentences.en: It's Caesar who organises the grain supply and it's Caesar who keeps the masses entertained, who provides the gladiatorial shows and so on.
sentences.zh: 是凯撒组织了粮食供应，是凯撒娱乐了大众，提供了角斗士表演等等。

sentences.en: So they likewise don't really want a republic.
sentences.zh: 所以他们同样不怎么想要一个共和国。

sentences.en: So let's get back to this moment of the curtain.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到这个拉开帷幕的时刻。

sentences.en: This bloke in the Palatine, Praetorian, he sees these feet sticking out under the curtain.
sentences.zh: 这个在帕拉蒂尼山的家伙，一个近卫军，看到有双脚从窗帘下面伸出来。

sentences.en: He takes Claudius to the Praetorian camp and presumably the Praetorians at this point are thinking of Claudius purely as their puppet.
sentences.zh: 他把克劳迪乌斯带到了近卫军军营，想必当时的近卫军把克劳迪乌斯纯粹当作他们的傀儡来对待。

sentences.en: He's somebody from the family, so they feel a sentimental attachment perhaps and they think we need a figurehead.
sentences.zh: 他是家族里的人，所以他们或许有一种情感上的依恋，觉得我们需要一个名义上的领袖。

sentences.en: Here's this bloke.
sentences.zh: 这不就是个现成的人选吗。

sentences.en: Who cares what his backstory is?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎他的背景是什么？

sentences.en: He's got the right bloodline.
sentences.zh: 他有着正统的血统。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Bring him in.
sentences.zh: 把他带进来。

sentences.en: Well, we'll discuss in due course, I think, whether it's just luck or whether it's perhaps something slightly more organised.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我们随后会讨论，这究竟只是运气，还是稍微有些组织性的结果。

sentences.en: But yes, you're right.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，你说得对。

sentences.en: They find Claudius.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了克劳迪乌斯。

sentences.en: Claudius is a part of the Auguste family.
sentences.zh: 克劳迪乌斯是奥古斯都家族的成员。

sentences.en: He's quite old by this point.
sentences.zh: 此时他已经不年轻了。

sentences.en: He's born in 10 BC.
sentences.zh: 他出生于公元前10年。

sentences.en: So Caligula's murdered in 41.
sentences.zh: 所以卡利古拉在公元41年被谋杀。

sentences.en: So he's into his 50s.
sentences.zh: 所以他已经五十多岁了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And people may be wondering, well, I mean, if he's in his 50s, he's a member of the
sentences.zh: 人们可能会纳闷，好吧，如果他已经五十多岁了，又是奥古斯都家族的成员，为什么他之前没有当上皇帝？

sentences.en: Auguste family, why hasn't he become emperor before?
sentences.zh: 为什么他不是显而易见的人选？

sentences.en: Why isn't he the obvious candidate?
sentences.zh: 我想，如果他是一个替代皇帝的人选，为什么卡利古拉没有杀了他？

sentences.en: And I suppose, you know, why hasn't Caligula killed him if he's an alternative emperor?
sentences.zh: 为什么卡利古拉没有杀了他？

sentences.en: And actually, I said he's got the right bloodline, but that's not quite right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 其实，我刚才说他有正确的血统，但这并不完全准确，对吧？

sentences.en: Because now it comes back to this issue that Suetonius was very interested in with Caligula,
sentences.zh: 因为现在这又回到了苏维托尼乌斯对卡利古拉非常感兴趣的那个问题上，

sentences.en: which really loomed large for Suetonius then, and I guess must do now again, which is exactly whom are you descended from?
sentences.zh: 这个问题对当时的苏维托尼乌斯来说至关重要，我想现在也一定如此，那就是你究竟是谁的后代？

sentences.en: Yeah, this really, really matters.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的非常非常重要。

sentences.en: So who is Claudius?
sentences.zh: 那么克劳迪乌斯是谁？

sentences.en: So to answer that, we need to go back to the scandalous marriage that Augustus had with this woman called Livia.
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我们需要回顾一下奥古斯都与一个叫莉薇娅的女人那场声名狼藉的婚姻。

sentences.en: So Livia is a Claudian.
sentences.zh: 莉薇娅是个克劳狄家族的人。

sentences.en: She had previously been married to another Claudian.
sentences.zh: 她之前曾嫁给另一个克劳狄家族的人。

sentences.en: She'd had a baby boy, Tiberius.
sentences.zh: 她生过一个男孩，叫提比略。

sentences.en: She's then pregnant by her first husband when Augustus decides he really wants her and marries her.
sentences.zh: 当奥古斯都决定他真心想要她并娶她时，她正怀着前夫的孩子。

sentences.en: He's in a position to obviously impose his will.
sentences.zh: 他显然有能力强加自己的意愿。

sentences.en: So Livia is massively pregnant when she marries Augustus.
sentences.zh: 所以莉薇娅嫁给奥古斯都时怀着身孕。

sentences.en: And shortly afterwards, she gives birth to a second son who is called Drusus.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，她生下了第二个儿子，名叫德鲁苏斯。

sentences.en: And Drusus, like Tiberius, is a tremendous war hero.
sentences.zh: 德鲁苏斯和提比略一样，是一位伟大的战争英雄。

sentences.en: He's entrusted by Augustus with assorted German campaigns.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都委任他指挥各种日耳曼战役。

sentences.en: He invades so far east that he reaches the line of the Elba, where he sees the ghostly apparition of a huge woman telling him to turn back.
sentences.zh: 他向东深入，甚至到达了易北河一线，在那里他看到了一个巨大女性的幻影，告诉他回去。

sentences.en: But he's very dashing, very heroic.
sentences.zh: 但他非常潇洒，非常英雄气概。

sentences.en: And then he dies young, which of course confirms his kind of reputation in the hearts of the
sentences.zh: 然后他英年早逝，这当然巩固了他在罗马人民心中的声誉。

sentences.en: Roman people.
sentences.zh: 罗马人民。

sentences.en: And it's all kind of very, you know, early years of Rome in a story by Livy.
sentences.zh: 这一切都有点像李维故事中罗马的早年岁月。

sentences.en: Tiberius escorts the corpse of his brother back to Rome on foot, weeping the whole way.
sentences.zh: 提比略步行护送他兄弟的尸体回罗马，一路上都在哭泣。

sentences.en: Very, very kind of heroic tableau.
sentences.zh: 非常有英雄气概的群像浮雕。

sentences.en: So Drusus is much admired, much loved.
sentences.zh: 所以德鲁苏斯备受尊崇与爱戴。

sentences.en: And fortunately, he has given the Roman people another war hero because Drusus is the father of Germanicus, who we talked about in the previous episode, the father of Caligula.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，他又为罗马人民带来了一位战争英雄，因为德鲁苏斯正是日耳曼尼库斯的父亲——我们在上一集中聊过他——也就是卡利古拉的父亲。

sentences.en: Very dashing, perfect in every way, apart from his spindly legs.
sentences.zh: 英姿飒爽，可以说是完美无缺，除了他的细长腿。

sentences.en: Absolute war hero again.
sentences.zh: 绝对又是一位战争英雄。

sentences.en: And everyone loves him.
sentences.zh: 而且大家都非常喜爱他。

sentences.en: However, Germanicus is not Drusus' only son.
sentences.zh: 然而，德鲁苏斯并不只有一个儿子。

sentences.en: So he has a second son.
sentences.zh: 所以他还有第二个儿子。

sentences.en: And this is Claudius.
sentences.zh: 这就是克劳狄乌斯。

sentences.en: And Claudius, as we said, is born in 10 BC, the 1st of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 而克劳狄乌斯正如我们所说，出生于公元前10年8月1日。

sentences.en: At Lucdunum, which is Lyon in Gaul, the kind of the great cult centre for the Augustan cult in Gaul.
sentences.zh: 在卢克敦姆，也就是高卢的里昂，这里可以说是高卢奥古斯都崇拜的核心圣地。

sentences.en: And Claudius is born.
sentences.zh: 就这样，克劳狄乌斯出生了。

sentences.en: Drusus dies the following year in 9 BC.
sentences.zh: 德鲁苏斯在第二年，即公元前9年去世了。

sentences.en: And so the infant Claudius is raised by his mother, Antonia, who is the daughter of Mark
sentences.zh: 因此，年幼的克劳狄乌斯由他的母亲安东尼娅抚养长大，安东尼娅是马克·安东尼的

sentences.en: Antony.
sentences.zh: 女儿。

sentences.en: So just to recap for people who don't know the family tree in front of them.
sentences.zh: 为了给那些对家族谱系不太了解的听众做个简单回顾。

sentences.en: Claudius is the nephew of Tiberius.
sentences.zh: 克劳狄乌斯是提比略的侄子。

sentences.en: He is the brother of Germanicus, who never got to become emperor.
sentences.zh: 他是日耳曼尼库斯的兄弟，而日耳曼尼库斯生前未能当上皇帝。

sentences.en: He's also the grandson of Mark Antony.
sentences.zh: 他也是马克·安东尼的孙子。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very well connected.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的背景非常显赫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's the step-grandson of Antony's great rival, the 1st Emperor Augustus.
sentences.zh: 他还是安东尼最大的死敌、第一位皇帝奥古斯都的继外孙。

sentences.en: So he has all kinds of connections, although the crucial one, the one with Augustus, is not a blood connection.
sentences.zh: 所以他有着各种各样的关系，尽管最关键的那一层——与奥古斯都的关系——并不是血亲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that wouldn't be an absolutely hopeless problem because Tiberius wasn't, but he gets adopted.
sentences.zh: 这本来也不是什么绝对无解的难题，因为提比略也不是血亲，但他被收养了。

sentences.en: And in the Roman system, if you get adopted, then you do become the son.
sentences.zh: 在罗马的体制下，如果你被收养了，那你就是名正言顺的儿子。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no, you know, I mean, as good as being a kind of blood son.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全可以说是……呃，和亲生儿子一样好。

sentences.en: So it would have been possible for Augustus or Tiberius at some point to have adopted Claudius, but they don't.
sentences.zh: 所以奥古斯都或提比略在某个时候完全有可能收养克劳狄乌斯，但他们并没有这么做。

sentences.en: And why do they not?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Well, the words of Suetonius.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们引用苏埃托尼乌斯的话。

sentences.en: For almost the entire length of his childhood and adolescence, he suffered from a range of chronic illnesses.
sentences.zh: 在他几乎整个童年和青春期里，他都饱受各种慢性疾病的折磨。

sentences.en: These left him so impaired, both mentally and physically, that even once he had come of age, he was regarded as unfitted for either public or private duties.
sentences.zh: 这些疾病使他在身心两方面都严重受损，以至于即使在他成年之后，人们仍认为他不适合担任任何公共或私人职务。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what are these illnesses?
sentences.zh: 那这些都是些什么病呢？

sentences.en: Well, so Suetonius goes on to list them.
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯接着列举了它们。

sentences.en: He has weak knees, which gives him a kind of hobbling, almost kind of limping gait.
sentences.zh: 他膝盖虚弱，这导致他的步伐踉踉跄跄，几乎像是在一瘸一拐。

sentences.en: His laughter, Suetonius says, is an unbecoming bray.
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯说，他的笑声是一种极其难听的驴叫声。

sentences.en: So a bit like Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 这有点像卡马拉·哈里斯。

sentences.en: I was about to say Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 我正想说卡马拉·哈里斯呢。

sentences.en: People gave her a lot of hard time, but I didn't mind her laugh, actually.
sentences.zh: 大家以前经常拿她开玩笑，但其实我并不介意她的笑声。

sentences.en: I thought it was quite endearing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得还挺可爱的。

sentences.en: Well, you might have liked Claudius's then.
sentences.zh: 那你可能也会喜欢克劳狄乌斯的笑声了。

sentences.en: But I wouldn't say hers was a bray.
sentences.zh: 但我不会说她的笑声是驴叫。

sentences.en: If his was a bray, I would dislike it because I don't like a braying laugh.
sentences.zh: 如果他的笑声是驴叫，我肯定会讨厌，因为我最讨厌像驴叫一样的笑声了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, Suetonius says it was a bray.
sentences.zh: 总之，苏埃托尼乌斯说那就是驴叫。

sentences.en: So obviously it was.
sentences.zh: 那显然就是了。

sentences.en: Because Suetonius is never wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为苏埃托尼乌斯从不出错。

sentences.en: Suetonius says he stammers and twitches.
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯说他口吃而且会抽搐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when he gets angry, he drooled and snorted mucus.
sentences.zh: 而且他一生气就会流口水、吸鼻涕。

sentences.en: And I hate that in a man, Tom, the snorting of mucus.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我最讨厌男人吸鼻涕了。

sentences.en: And apparently Claudius gets angry quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 显然克劳狄乌斯经常生气。

sentences.en: So there's quite a lot of snot flying around the palatine.
sentences.zh: 所以帕拉蒂尼山宫殿里到处都是飞溅的鼻涕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So clearly he suffers from various ailments and disadvantages.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他饱受各种病痛和先天劣势的折磨。

sentences.en: And people might be wondering, well, do his grandmother, Livia, and his mother, Antonia, show him sympathy and compassion?
sentences.zh: 人们或许会想，那他的祖母莉维亚和母亲安东尼娅会对他表现出同情和怜悯吗？

sentences.en: Or are they monstrously ableist?
sentences.zh: 还是说她们有着可怕的健全主义偏见？

sentences.en: And I'm afraid to say that they are monstrously ableiSt.
sentences.zh: 我很遗憾地告诉大家，她们确实有着可怕的健全主义偏见。

sentences.en: Oh, that's disappointing.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真令人失望。

sentences.en: So Livia is so mortified by having this grandson who kind of twitches and limps and blows snot everywhere that she can barely bring herself to talk to him and generally communicates with him by kind of sending him written missives.
sentences.zh: 莉维亚对拥有这样一个会抽搐、瘸腿、到处甩鼻涕的孙子感到无比羞耻，以至于她几乎无法面对面和他说话，通常都是通过写信来跟他沟通。

sentences.en: And again, to quote Suetonius, his mother, Antonia, used to describe him as a monstrosity of a human being, begun by nature, but only half finished,
sentences.zh: 再次引用苏埃托尼乌斯的话，他的母亲安东尼娅过去常把他描述为一个“人类的怪物，由大自然开头，却只完成了一半”，

sentences.en: and would accuse anyone whose stupidity she particularly wished to emphasise of being a bigger fool than her son, Claudius.
sentences.zh: 并且每当她想强调某人的愚蠢时，就会指责对方是个比她儿子克劳狄乌斯还要大的笨蛋。

sentences.en: But actually, I'll tell you who's really nice to him, and this bears out my view, that actually I think you're very hard on this person and you paint him in an unduly dark light,
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我来告诉你谁对他真正好，这也印证了我的观点——我觉得你对这个人太苛刻了，把他描绘得过于黑暗，

sentences.en: and that is Augustus.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是奥古斯都。

sentences.en: Augustus is ultimately a kind man and is lovely to Claudius.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都本质上是个善良的人，对克劳狄乌斯非常好。

sentences.en: Except when filtering senators.
sentences.zh: 除了清洗元老院议员的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, but who cares about them?
sentences.zh: 对，但谁会在乎他们？

sentences.en: He's very nice to Claudius, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他对克劳狄乌斯非常好，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's very nice to Claudius.
sentences.zh: 他对克劳狄乌斯非常好。

sentences.en: He's not very nice to Claudius.
sentences.zh: 他才对克劳狄乌斯不好呢。

sentences.en: Yeah, but compare with the rest of the family, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，跟家里其他人比比看嘛。

sentences.en: I mean, he's nicer than his mother, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他肯定比克劳狄乌斯的母亲要好。

sentences.en: I mean, Augustus agrees that it would be embarrassing to his regime to have Claudius kind of exposed to the public eye.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都确实认为，让克劳狄乌斯暴露在公众视野中会让自己政权脸上无光。

sentences.en: But he does kind of recognise qualities in Claudius.
sentences.zh: 但他确实看出了克劳狄乌斯身上的某些特质。

sentences.en: Read, Tom, to the listeners what Augustus wrote about him.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，给听众们读读奥古斯都对他的评价吧。

sentences.en: Right, so this is a letter quoted by Suetonius.
sentences.zh: 好的，这是苏埃托尼乌斯引用的一封信。

sentences.en: I mean, I love it when Suetonius quotes letters.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢苏埃托尼乌斯引用书信的时候。

sentences.en: You feel, you know, really up close.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得历史真的近在咫尺。

sentences.en: And yeah, Augustus wrote to Livia,
sentences.zh: 是的，奥古斯都写信给莉维亚说：

sentences.en: The poor boy has been cheated by fortune, for in significant matters, when he can hold his concentration, the nobility of his spirit is evident enough.
sentences.zh: “这个可怜的孩子被命运捉弄了，因为在谈到重要事情时，只要他能集中注意力，他灵魂中的高贵就足够显而易见。”

sentences.en: Quarter at demonstrandum.
sentences.zh: 实地证明完毕。

sentences.en: There's another letter where he says,
sentences.zh: 还有另一封信，他在信中说：

sentences.en: It's amazing, I went to hear Claudius give a talk about some academic subject, and it was brilliant.
sentences.zh: “太神奇了，我去听克劳狄乌斯做关于某个学术课题的演讲，讲得真是太精彩了。”

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Okay, now, you said to give a talk about this academic subject.
sentences.zh: 好啦，你刚才说他做了关于这个学术课题的演讲。

sentences.en: Now, it's true, you can be academically very prominent and a complete and utter fool.
sentences.zh: 现在，确实有人可以在学术上非常显赫，但同时却是个彻头彻尾的笨蛋。

sentences.en: And I think we can all think of people who tick that particular box.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都能想到符合这一特定标准的人。

sentences.en: But you, this business that Antonia said, oh, anyone who's really stupid, I call him a bigger fool than Claudius.
sentences.zh: 但是，安东尼娅说过的那种话——“哦，谁要是真蠢，我就说他比克劳狄乌斯更蠢”——

sentences.en: And Claudius is an absolute dribbling idiot.
sentences.zh: 而克劳狄乌斯是个流着口水的绝对白痴。

sentences.en: If he's a dribbling idiot, how is it he's giving academic lectures?
sentences.zh: 如果他是个流着口水的白痴，他又怎么能去做学术讲座呢？

sentences.en: I mean, again, people who've spent time at our great universities may find that question easy to answer.
sentences.zh: 当然，在我们的名牌大学里待过的人可能会觉得这个问题很容易回答。

sentences.en: But no doubt you'll have your own answer, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，汤姆，你会有你自己的答案。

sentences.en: I think that it is a kind of general assumption in the Greek and Roman world that if you look like an idiot, you are an idiot.
sentences.zh: 我认为希腊和罗马世界普遍有一种假设：如果你看起来像个白痴，那你就是个白痴。

sentences.en: That's the kind of core assumption.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种核心假设。

sentences.en: They're not very woke at all on such matters.
sentences.zh: 在这方面他们可一点都不“觉醒”（woke）。

sentences.en: But it's evident that Claudius, despite sending streams of snot everywhere when he gets cross, is very intellectual, academically able.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，克劳狄乌斯尽管一生气就会四处喷射鼻涕，却极具才华，学术能力很强。

sentences.en: So he's fluent in Greek.
sentences.zh: 所以他精通希腊语。

sentences.en: He's very knowledgeable about literature and precisely because he's not allowed to enjoy a public life.
sentences.zh: 他对文学知识渊博，恰恰是因为他不被允许享受公众生活。

sentences.en: You know, he's not allowed to go and follow in the footsteps of Germanicus and lead expeditions into Germany.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他不能去追随日耳曼尼库斯的脚步，去日耳曼率领远征军。

sentences.en: So that gives him the chance to spend, or I guess if you're a Roman aristocrat, waste his time on scholarly pursuits.
sentences.zh: 这反倒给了他机会把时间花在——或者如果你是个罗马贵族的话，可以说是浪费时间在——学术追求上。

sentences.en: And the mark, I guess, of how much he wastes his time, of how contemptible a figure he is by the standards of the Roman aristocracy, is that actually he becomes a historian.
sentences.zh: 我想，从他浪费了多少时间、以及按罗马贵族的标准来看他是一个多么遭人鄙视的人物来看，最典型的标志就是他最终成了一名历史学家。

sentences.en: So he's a total loser.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个彻头彻尾的失败者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A slobbering, twitching, socially incompetent historian.
sentences.zh: 一个流着口水、抽搐着、社交无能的历史学家。

sentences.en: Who would have thought it?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: Thank goodness there are none of those left anymore, Tom.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，现在这种人已经绝种了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, and Dominic, the other, I mean, possible point of comparison with historians that certainly I know is that he writes enormously long books.
sentences.zh: 而且多米尼克，据我所知，他与历史学家的另一个相似之处在于，他写出了极其皇皇巨著。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 不会吧。

sentences.en: So his editor says, so here's a commission to write a history of the Etruscans.
sentences.zh: 所以他的编辑说：好吧，这里有个任务，写一部伊特鲁里亚史。

sentences.en: Could you keep it down to two books?
sentences.zh: 你能把它控制在两本书的篇幅内吗？

sentences.en: And he writes 20 books.
sentences.zh: 然后他写了20卷。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 不会吧。

sentences.en: And he gets a commission to write a history of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 结果他接到了编写迦太基史的任务。

sentences.en: Make it one book.
sentences.zh: 写成一本书吧。

sentences.en: Eight books.
sentences.zh: 结果他写了8卷。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's good to write an improperly immersive, well-textured history.
sentences.zh: 有时候，写一部引人入胜、质感丰富的宏大历史是件好事。

sentences.en: And that takes multiple volumes.
sentences.zh: 而这需要多卷本才能完成。

sentences.en: What can I say?
sentences.zh: 我还能说什么呢？

sentences.en: With chapters on snooker.
sentences.zh: 里面甚至还有关于斯诺克的章节。

sentences.en: And do you know, Claudius would have loved all that because he's very, he writes a book about dice.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，克劳狄乌斯肯定会喜欢这些，因为他非常博学，他还写过一本关于骰子的书。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, he's interested in pretty much everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他几乎对所有事情都感兴趣。

sentences.en: And he's a historian.
sentences.zh: 而且他是一名历史学家。

sentences.en: He's a contemporary historian.

sentences.zh: 再次如你所说，他其实并没有亲自率军。

sentences.en: But once Britain has, you know, the bridgehead has been established and Colchester is on the verge of falling.
sentences.zh: 但一旦不列颠，你知道，桥头堡已经建立，科尔切斯特即将陷落之时，

sentences.en: Claudius goes over and he does it with elephants to create as big a splash as possible.
sentences.zh: 克劳狄乌斯便赶了过去，他带着大象一同前往，以造成尽可能轰动的效果。

sentences.en: And then when he comes back, he reenacts it.
sentences.zh: 当他回来后，他又将其重新演绎了一番。

sentences.en: So he presides over kind of various reenactments on the campus marshes, showing highlights from the campaign in Britain.
sentences.zh: 于是他主持了战神广场上的各种重演活动，展示了不列颠战役中的精彩片段。

sentences.en: You know, Colchester being stormed, various British kings surrendering.
sentences.zh: 你知道，科尔切斯特被攻陷，各不列颠国王纷纷投降。

sentences.en: And across the Mediterranean, he has himself portrayed as a kind of buff rapiSt.
sentences.zh: 在地中海各地，他把自己塑造成一个粗鲁的强暴者形象。

sentences.en: So there's this freeze from Aphrodisias in what's now Turkey, which shows him, which shows
sentences.zh: 比如来自如今土耳其境内的阿弗罗狄西亚斯的这幅浮雕，上面展示了

sentences.en: Britannia as a woman whose robes have been torn from her and Claudius as this kind of muscle bound guy who's forcing her to the ground.
sentences.zh: 不列颠尼亚化为一个长袍被撕裂的女性，而克劳狄乌斯则是一个肌肉健硕、将其强行按倒在地的男子。

sentences.en: And obviously, that's not how a politician today would want to be represented.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这并不是当今政客希望自己被塑造的形象。

sentences.en: But that's how, you know, it plays well with Roman audiences.
sentences.zh: 但这就是，你知道的，这在罗马观众中很吃香。

sentences.en: And it's clearly how Claudius wanted to be seen.
sentences.zh: 而且这显然正是克劳狄乌斯希望被看待的方式。

sentences.en: He's, you know, he's no longer the kind of elderly, stammering, twitching historian.
sentences.zh: 他，你知道，他不再是那个老态龙钟、结巴抽搐的历史学家。

sentences.en: He's a man of action who subdues provinces, subdues women.
sentences.zh: 他是一个征服行省、征服女性的行动派硬汉。

sentences.en: And he's a Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他是一位凯撒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's not just military, is it?
sentences.zh: 但不仅限于军事，对吧？

sentences.en: He likes a grand projet, public works, sort of a lot of hydraulic action, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢宏伟的工程、公共建设，可以说包含了相当多水利方面的动作。

sentences.en: So he's very into hydrology.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常热衷于水利学。

sentences.en: Another thing he'd written a book about, he'd written a book about canals in Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 这也是他写过书的另一个领域，他曾写过一本关于美索不达米亚运河的书。

sentences.en: God, that sounds fascinating.
sentences.zh: 天哪，听起来太迷人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Except, you know, grand projet, again, I mean, Caesar had been into that.
sentences.zh: 不过呢，宏伟工程这方面，凯撒也曾热衷于此。

sentences.en: Augustus had been into that.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都也曾热衷于此。

sentences.en: And the Claudians definitely had been into that.
sentences.zh: 而克劳狄家族绝对也对此乐此不疲。

sentences.en: So one of his most famous ancestors, Appius Claudius, had built the Appian Way, the great road that joins Rome to the kind of the heel of Italy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他最著名的祖先之一阿庇乌斯·克劳狄乌斯曾修建过亚壁古道，那条连接罗马与意大利“鞋跟”的大道。

sentences.en: And Claudius seems to be genuinely enthusiastic about taking up that battle of improving infrastructure in Rome.
sentences.zh: 而克劳狄乌斯似乎对承担改善罗马基础设施这一大业抱有真正的热情。

sentences.en: So the obvious thing that every emperor has to worry about is the grain supply.
sentences.zh: 所以每个皇帝都必须操心的显而易见的事情就是粮食供应。

sentences.en: And historically, it's been a problem that Rome does not have a deep sea port.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，罗马没有深水港一直是个大问题。

sentences.en: So at the mouth of the Tiber, this is Port Ostia, which I know, Dominic, you're a big fan of.
sentences.zh: 所以在台伯河口，这里就是奥斯提亚港，多米尼克，我知道你是这里的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you love it, don't you?
sentences.zh: 是的，你很喜欢它，对吧？

sentences.en: I think Ostia is one of the best places you can go.
sentences.zh: 我认为奥斯提亚是你去旅游的最佳地点之一。

sentences.en: If you go to Rome, my single recommendation to the listeners is to go to Ostia Antica.
sentences.zh: 如果你去罗马，我对听众的唯一建议就是去古奥斯提亚。

sentences.en: It's as good as Pompeii, and there's nobody else there.
sentences.zh: 它和庞贝一样棒，而且还没有什么游客。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: You've heard it.
sentences.zh: 你听到了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, Claudius would be thrilled to hear that, because he decides that he's going to build
sentences.zh: 克劳狄乌斯听到这个消息一定会非常高兴，因为他决定要

sentences.en: a massive deep sea port at the mouth of the Tiber, and when he summons engineers and tells them this is what he's going to do, they throw up their hands in horror and say, you
sentences.zh: 在台伯河口建造一座庞大的深水港。当他召集工程师并告诉他们这就是他的计划时，他们惊恐万分地举起双手说，

sentences.en: know, on no account to tempt this, it'll be a disaster.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，无论如何都不能尝试这个，这会是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It'll be a kind of HS2 fiasco.
sentences.zh: 这会变成一种类似高铁二期（HS2）式的惨败。

sentences.en: But, you know, Claudius is Caesar.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，克劳狄乌斯是凯撒。

sentences.en: He can do what he likes.
sentences.zh: 他想做什么就能做什么。

sentences.en: And if it serves the good of the Roman people to remold the land, to gouge out the bottom of the sea, then that's what he's going to do.
sentences.zh: 如果改造土地、掏空海底符合罗马人民的利益，那么他就会这么做。

sentences.en: And so he goes ahead.
sentences.zh: 于是他继续推进。

sentences.en: He also, he's a great man for an aqueduct.
sentences.zh: 而且，他也是一个非常热衷于修建引水渠的人。

sentences.en: He builds two enormous aqueducts, and one of them, the aqua Claudia, is probably the greatest of all Rome's aqueducts.
sentences.zh: 他建造了两条巨大的引水渠，其中一条——克劳狄乌斯引水渠，可能是罗马所有引水渠中最宏伟的一条。

sentences.en: And what's fascinating about them is that they, like Claudius, are simultaneously very modern and very ancient.
sentences.zh: 关于它们，最迷人的一点在于，它们就像克劳狄乌斯本人一样，既非常现代又极其古老。

sentences.en: So they're kind of cutting edge engineering, but they have the cladding of a kind of old school aqueduct.
sentences.zh: 所以它们采用了尖端的工程技术，却披着老派引水渠的外衣。

sentences.en: And I think that's a beautiful summation of what Claudius is about.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是对克劳狄乌斯特质的绝妙概括。

sentences.en: Efficiency, modernity, but dress it up to look old.
sentences.zh: 高效、现代，但却要装扮成古老的模样。

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically what I'd like as well, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不得不说，这基本上也是我想要的。

sentences.en: I'd be all in favour of that.
sentences.zh: 我会完全赞成这一点。

sentences.en: And these are recognised by contemporaries as being astonishing achievements.
sentences.zh: 同时代的人也承认这些是惊人的成就。

sentences.en: So Pliny the Elder, he writes that they are wonders without rival in the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，老普林尼写道，它们是世界上无可匹敌的奇迹。

sentences.en: And so obviously this redounds, again, greatly to Claudius's credit.
sentences.zh: 显然，这再次为克劳狄乌斯赢得了巨大的声誉。

sentences.en: Makes him very, very popular with the people who look to Caesar to keep them watered, to keep them fed.
sentences.zh: 这使他在那些指望凯撒让他们有水喝、有饭吃的人民中变得非常非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And it's also popular because it gives them jobs.
sentences.zh: 它之所以受欢迎，还因为它为他们提供了工作岗位。

sentences.en: So it's not slaves who are doing the work.
sentences.zh: 所以干活的不是奴隶。

sentences.en: It's the mass of the people.
sentences.zh: 而是广大民众。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of Keynesian scheme, I guess, you could say.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说，这是一种凯恩斯主义的计划。

sentences.en: Putting money into the economy.
sentences.zh: 向经济体注入资金。

sentences.en: Putting money into the economy.
sentences.zh: 向经济体注入资金。

sentences.en: So the other thing is that Claudius is not, although he's quite old school, he's not like a Tiberius kind of duh, killjoy who sneers at the pleasures of the populace.
sentences.zh: 所以另一件事是，克劳狄乌斯虽然相当老派，但他并不像提比略那种对大众的快乐嗤之以鼻的无趣死板之辈。

sentences.en: So you said Claudius would like a chapter on snooker.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才说克劳狄乌斯会喜欢一章关于斯诺克的书。

sentences.en: He'd enjoy a night out at a smoke-filled snooker hall.
sentences.zh: 他会很享受在烟雾缭绕的斯诺克球馆度过一个夜晚。

sentences.en: He absolutely would.
sentences.zh: 他绝对会喜欢的。

sentences.en: Yes, he absolutely would.
sentences.zh: 是的，他绝对会。

sentences.en: So I said, you know, he writes a book on gambling, which is seen as being a very de class A occupation.
sentences.zh: 所以我说过，他写了一本关于赌博的书，当时这被认为是一种非常低俗的消遣。

sentences.en: He enjoys the pleasures of the masses.
sentences.zh: 他享受大众的乐趣。

sentences.en: And in fact, he's so keen on gladiatorial combat that Suetonius writes that he is shockingly obsessed by executions, which in a kind of a day of spectacles in an amphitheater, the
sentences.zh: 事实上，他对手角斗士竞技是如此热衷，以至于苏维托尼乌斯写道，他极其痴迷于死刑处决。在圆形剧场里一整天的表演中，

sentences.en: climax would be gladiators.
sentences.zh: 高潮会是角斗士对决。

sentences.en: Then before that, you'd have the wild beasts.
sentences.zh: 而在那之前，会有猛兽表演。

sentences.en: And before that, you would have the executions.
sentences.zh: 再之前，会有处决犯人。

sentences.en: And the executions, it's kind of, you know, you've got to be an obsessive fan to go and watch them.
sentences.zh: 至于处决，你知道的，你得是个狂热粉丝才会去看。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Claudius is a kind of, you know, he does like to go and watch them.
sentences.zh: 而克劳狄乌斯，你知道的，他确实喜欢去看那些。

sentences.en: So it's like going to see a famous band or something and going to see the warm-up act.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像去看某个著名乐队或者去观看暖场表演一样。

sentences.en: The warm-up act.
sentences.zh: 暖场表演。

sentences.en: So going to the Olympics and going to watch like some terrible sport that you know interests him.
sentences.zh: 就像去参加奥运会，然后去看某些他感兴趣的糟糕比赛。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: It's unsurprising that a lot of the shows that he puts on are very, very famous.
sentences.zh: 毫不奇怪，他举办的许多表演都非常非常著名。

sentences.en: And in fact, one of them gives rise to perhaps one of the most famous sayings from the whole of Roman history.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一场表演诞生了整个罗马历史上最著名的名言之一。

sentences.en: He's trying to drain this lake in the countryside above Rome.
sentences.zh: 他当时正试图排干罗马郊外乡村的一座湖泊。

sentences.en: And to mark the final completion of this project before the canal is open that will drain the lake, he has a great sea battle staged there.
sentences.zh: 为了纪念这个项目的最后完成，在排干湖水的运河开通之前，他在那里举办了一场盛大的海战。

sentences.en: And all the gladiators who've been assembled onto the boats to stage this turn to Claudius where he's looking very kind of splendid.
sentences.zh: 所有被集合到船上以重现这一场景的角斗士们转向克劳狄乌斯，此时他看起来非常威风凛凛。

sentences.en: You know, he sat down looking tremendously imperious.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他坐着，看起来气宇轩昂。

sentences.en: And they say, hail Caesar, we who are about to die salute you.
sentences.zh: 他们说，凯撒万岁，我们这些即将死去的人向您致敬。

sentences.en: And that's where this is from.
sentences.zh: 这就是这句话的出处。

sentences.en: That is where that phrase has come from.
sentences.zh: 这正是那个短语的来源。

sentences.en: Although it's very, very Claudius that he then totally messes it up.
sentences.zh: 尽管这也非常符合克劳狄乌斯的风格，他随后把事情彻底搞砸了。

sentences.en: So when they say we're about to die salute you, he replies or not, because, you know, maybe some of them will, won't die.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们说我们即将死去向您致敬时，他回答或者不，因为，你知道的，也许他们中的一些人会、不会死。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of very Don-ish, very waspish humour or not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种非常牛津学者风范、非常尖酸刻薄的幽默或者说不一定。

sentences.en: And so all the gladiators hear him say that.
sentences.zh: 于是所有的角斗士都听到他这么说。

sentences.en: And so they think, oh, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想，哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: He's pardoning us.
sentences.zh: 他赦免我们了。

sentences.en: We don't have to fight.
sentences.zh: 我们不用打了。

sentences.en: And so they kind of put down their weapons and refuse to fight.
sentences.zh: 于是他们放下了武器，拒绝战斗。

sentences.en: And Claudius is so outraged by this that he gets up out of his throne and hurries down to yell at them and tell them to get a move on.
sentences.zh: 克劳狄乌斯对此愤怒已极，以至于他从王座上站起来，匆忙走下去大声训斥他们，叫他们动作快点。

sentences.en: And of course, when he does that, he hobbles and limps.
sentences.zh: 当然，当他这样做时，他一瘸一拐地走着。

sentences.en: And the impression of majesty and splendor is compromised.
sentences.zh: 那种威严和辉煌的印象大打折扣。

sentences.en: However, he does manage to persuade the guys to the gladiators to pick up their weapons.
sentences.zh: 不过，他确实成功说服了这群人——这些角斗士重新拿起武器。

sentences.en: And so the fight goes ahead.
sentences.zh: 于是战斗继续进行了。

sentences.en: That's good news for the crowd.
sentences.zh: 这对观众来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: Good news for the crowd.
sentences.zh: 对观众来说是好消息。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Maybe less good news for the gladiators.
sentences.zh: 对角斗士来说可能就没那么好了。

sentences.en: Now, there is, of course, a problem with this, which is that it's very expensive.
sentences.zh: 现在，这里当然存在一个问题，那就是这非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And that is compounded by the fact that Claudius' predecessor, Caligula, had also been very keen on lavishing money on, you know, extravaganzas.
sentences.zh: 再加上另一个情况，克劳狄乌斯的前任卡利古拉也极度热衷于将大量资金挥霍在各种穷奢极欲的盛会上。

sentences.en: So the treasury is pretty bare.
sentences.zh: 所以国库已经相当空虚了。

sentences.en: But Claudius is very proactive.
sentences.zh: 但克劳狄乌斯非常有进取心。

sentences.en: And again, I think he's clearly thought about what he's going to do.
sentences.zh: 再次证明，我认为他显然仔细考虑过自己要做什么。

sentences.en: And he wants to set the administration of the household of Caesar on as firm a footing as he can,
sentences.zh: 他希望将凯撒皇室的行政管理建立在尽可能稳固的基础上，

sentences.en: because he recognizes that that administration is also effectively the administration of the entire empire.
sentences.zh: 因为他认识到，这一行政管理实际上也就是整个帝国的行政管理。

sentences.en: So until Claudius,
sentences.zh: 所以在克劳狄乌斯之前，

sentences.en: the fact that Caesar needs money because the money that he has is basically the income that keeps the empire running had been disguised or at least hadn't properly been acknowledged.
sentences.zh: 凯撒需要资金——因为他拥有的资金基本上是维持帝国运转的收入——这一事实一直被掩盖，或者至少没有得到应有的承认。

sentences.en: But Claudius, perhaps because, you know, the circumstances in which he's come to power, you know, he's more like, you know,
sentences.zh: 但克劳狄乌斯，也许是因为他登基的背景，你知道的，他更像是一个，

sentences.en: a military strongman who's come to power in a coup than a kind of hereditary monarch.
sentences.zh: 通过政变上台的军事强人，而不是某种世袭君主。

sentences.en: You know, he's kind of unabashed about the need to make his administration as streamlined and efficient as possible.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他对于需要让自己的行政机构尽可能精简和高效这一点，表现得毫不掩饰。

sentences.en: And so the people he turns to for that are the people that any wealthy Roman who needs specialists would turn to.
sentences.zh: 因此，他为此求助的人，正是任何需要专家的富裕罗马人都会求助的人。

sentences.en: And these are people who are slaves or freedmen, because as Caesar, he has the pick of the ablest, smartest people, you know,
sentences.zh: 这些人就是奴隶或解放自由民，因为作为凯撒，他拥有挑选最有能力、最聪明的人的特权，你知道的，

sentences.en: Greeks with particular specialisms in various fields of finance or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如在金融等各个领域拥有特殊专长的希腊人。

sentences.en: And so these freedmen are basically entrusted by Claudius with the running of the empire.
sentences.zh: 所以克劳狄乌斯基本上把帝国的运营托付给了这些解放自由民。

sentences.en: And they prove to be very, very effective at it.
sentences.zh: 事实证明他们干得非常非常出色。

sentences.en: So these are the people like anyone who's read I, Claudius will remember Narcissus and Pallas and people like that who presumably they're very bright and they're very good.
sentences.zh: 这些人就像读过《我，克劳狄乌斯》的人都会记得的纳西索斯、帕拉斯之流，想必他们非常聪明而且能力卓越。

sentences.en: But I would guess they must attract a lot of haters, of course, because everyone in the Senate is massively resentful.
sentences.zh: 但我想他们肯定也会招来很多嫉恨，因为元老院里的所有人都满怀怨恨。

sentences.en: And of course, it also plays into the stereotype of Claudius as a, you know, a foolish old man who is easily manipulated and dominated by people who properly should, you know,
sentences.zh: 当然，这也符合对克劳狄乌斯的刻板印象，即他是一个愚蠢的老头，很容易被那些本来应该，你知道的，

sentences.en: be kept firmly under thumb of whom slaves and freedmen would be the paradigm.
sentences.zh: 被牢牢掌控在手心的人所操纵和支配，而奴隶和解放自由民就是这种人的典范。

sentences.en: So under the thumb, as he was of these men, so that's the freedmen, the favourites, he played the part not of a princeps, but of a flunky,
sentences.zh: 因此，就像他受制于这些男人（也就是那些解放自由民、近臣）一样，他扮演的角色不是元首，而是一个随从，

sentences.en: dispensing magistracies here and military commands there, pardoning and punishing people, largely oblivious to how much he was the creature of this or that favourite's interests.
sentences.zh: 在这里分发官职，在那里颁发军事指挥权，宽恕和惩罚人们，对于自己有多大程度上沦为了这个或那个宠臣利益的傀儡却浑然不觉。

sentences.en: So this is a crucial part of the image of Claudius, that he's an idiot who essentially is so feeble minded that he's become the plaything of his favourites.
sentences.zh: 所以这是克劳狄乌斯形象中至关重要的一部分，即他是个白痴，本质上头脑极其简单，以至于成了宠臣们的玩物。

sentences.en: Now, we know that's not true because in Egypt we found, when I say we, I mean scholars, archaeologists,
sentences.zh: 现在，我们知道这不是真的，因为我们在埃及发现——当我指“我们”时，我是指学者、考古学家——

sentences.en: have found documentary evidence for the close attention that Claudius plays to the administration of his empire and the kind of the evident intelligence with which he corresponds to people in provinces across the span of the Roman world.
sentences.zh: 发现了文献证据，证明克劳狄乌斯对帝国的行政管理给予了高度关注，并且从他与罗马世界各地省份民众的通信中可以看出他具备明显的智慧。

sentences.en: He's a very smart, he's a very smart, able guy and actually the fact he has all these freedmen serving him, now this isn't evidence of his senility or imbecility,
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常聪明、非常有能力的人，事实上他让所有这些解放自由民为他服务，这并不是他衰老或痴呆的证据，

sentences.en: it's evidence of his astute ability to marshal innovation.
sentences.zh: 而是他善于运用创新的敏锐能力的证明。

sentences.en: But part of what makes his contemporaries and posterity assume that Claudius is feeble minded is that there's a sense that he's under the thumb not just of freedmen,
sentences.zh: 但让他的同代人和后人误以为克劳狄乌斯头脑简单的一部分原因在于，人们觉得他不仅受制于解放自由民，

sentences.en: but also even worse of women, and particularly of a succession of wives of whom perhaps the most notorious is a woman called Messalina.
sentences.zh: 甚至更糟的是受制于女人，特别是接连几任妻子，其中最臭名昭著的也许是一个叫麦萨利娜的女人。

sentences.en: Now, I was hoping we'd get on to Messalina.
sentences.zh: 我本来就希望我们能聊到麦萨利娜。

sentences.en: So Messalina is, he basically has his pick, I guess, does he?
sentences.zh: 所以麦萨利娜是，他基本上可以随心所欲地挑选，对吧？

sentences.en: And he picks a very young, beautiful and crucially very blue-blooded wife.
sentences.zh: 他挑选了一个非常年轻、美丽而且至关重要的出身名门的妻子。

sentences.en: I think it's the blue-blooded that matters.
sentences.zh: 我认为出身名门才是最重要的。

sentences.en: I think the beauty and youth is, you know, these are perks.
sentences.zh: 我认为美貌和年轻，你知道的，这些只是额外的好处。

sentences.en: She's the great-grandniece of Augustus, right?
sentences.zh: 她是奥古斯都的曾孙女，对吧？

sentences.en: So she helps him to sort of say, I'm the heir to the greatest emperor, the first emperor.
sentences.zh: 所以她帮助他宣称：我是最伟大皇帝、第一位皇帝的继承人。

sentences.en: And that is a crucial role that she plays.
sentences.zh: 这是她扮演的一个至关重要的角色。

sentences.en: And it gives her a certain degree of independent power.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了她某种程度的独立权力。

sentences.en: Because everyone, I mean, Claudius knows, and everyone else knows, that being married to Messalina, who is the great-grandniece of Augustus, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为每个人，我是说，克劳狄乌斯知道，其他所有人也都知道，娶了身为奥古斯都曾孙女的麦萨利娜，

sentences.en: this is a crucial buttressing of his status and prestige.
sentences.zh: 这是对他地位和威望的一个关键支柱。

sentences.en: And her significance and her kind of independence of operation is enhanced by the fact that in AD41, she gives him crucially a male heir.
sentences.zh: 而在公元41年，她为他生下了一个至关重要的男性继承人，这进一步提升了她的重要性和她某种程度上的行动独立性。

sentences.en: So he now has a son who can inherit this, you know, his role in the House of Caesar.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在有了一个儿子，可以继承他在凯撒家族中的角色。

sentences.en: With a great name.
sentences.zh: 带着一个伟大的名字。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So two years later, Claudius presides over the conquest of Britain.
sentences.zh: 两年后，克劳狄乌斯主持了对不列颠的征服。

sentences.en: And so this little boy gets given the name of Britannicus.
sentences.zh: 于是这个小男孩被赋予了不列颠尼库斯的名字。

sentences.en: And Messalina's role in this, you know, crucial.
sentences.zh: 麦萨利娜在这其中的角色，你知道的，至关重要。

sentences.en: And so she has basically made herself fundamental, not just to the status of Claudius' regime as it exists in the present, but its prospects in the future.
sentences.zh: 因此，她基本上让自己变得不可或缺，不仅对克劳狄乌斯政权在眼下的地位如此，对其未来的前景也是如此。

sentences.en: Basically, it's kind of, it's perpetuation.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这就是它的延续。

sentences.en: And so it's unsurprising that she is portrayed in statues as the very model of a sober, respectable Roman matron.
sentences.zh: 所以毫不奇怪，她在雕像中被描绘成了一个端庄、体面的罗马主妇的典范。

sentences.en: And she's praised as the absolute model of Roman womanhood.
sentences.zh: 她被誉为罗马女性气质的绝对典范。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, dear listeners, here's the question.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，亲爱的听众们，问题来了。

sentences.en: Is she the model of Roman womanhood?
sentences.zh: 她真的是罗马女性气质的典范吗？

sentences.en: Or is she an outrageous strumpet?
sentences.zh: 还是她是一个放荡的荡妇？

sentences.en: Well, if you've seen or indeed read by Claudius, you will remember that there is, I mean, it's one of the great scandals, not just in Roman history, but all history, when Claudius,
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你看过或者读过《我，克劳狄乌斯》，你就会记得，这是罗马历史上乃至全部历史上最大的丑闻之一：当克劳狄乌斯

sentences.en: he's at Ostia, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 在奥斯蒂亚时，对吧？

sentences.en: He's looking around that splendid site that I was recommending to the listeners.
sentences.zh: 他在参观我向听众推荐的那个壮丽遗址。

sentences.en: And if the Ostia tourist board want to get in touch, I'd be very keen to hear from them.
sentences.zh: 如果奥斯蒂亚旅游局想联系我们，我很乐意听取他们的意见。

sentences.en: So he's looking around Ostia and somebody, a concubine of his, comes up to him and says, Messalina is carrying on behind your back.
sentences.zh: 所以他正在参观奥斯蒂亚，他的一位妃嫔走过来对他说，麦萨利娜在你的背地里胡作非为。

sentences.en: And not just carrying on, she's up to all sorts, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是胡作非为，汤姆，她正在搞各种名堂。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, she's having an affair with this very good looking young senator who's also very ambitious.
sentences.zh: 对，她和这个非常英俊且野心勃勃的年轻元老有了外遇。

sentences.en: And the story is, is that they're conspiring to replace Claudius as emperor.
sentences.zh: 故事是说，他们正在密谋取代克劳狄乌斯成为皇帝。

sentences.en: And in fact, that Messalina has married this guy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，麦萨利娜已经和这个人结婚了。

sentences.en: And, you know, she's the great grandniece of Augustus and she's the mother of Britannicus.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，她是奥古斯都的曾孙女，又是不列颠尼库斯的母亲。

sentences.en: So this is potentially, you know, if it's true, very, very dangerous for Claudius.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这是真的，这可能会对克劳狄乌斯造成非常非常大的危险。

sentences.en: And the measure of his alarm is that he goes speeding back to Rome and he doesn't go to the Palatine,
sentences.zh: 他感到惊慌的程度从他急忙赶回罗马可见一斑，他没有去帕拉蒂尼山，

sentences.en: but he goes to the Praetorian camp because he's got to, clearly he's worried, you know,
sentences.zh: 而是去了近卫军军营，因为他必须这样做，显然他很担心，

sentences.en: he needs to make sure that that's secure because only if that's secure can he then take measures to deal with this threat.
sentences.zh: 他需要确保那里是安全的，只有确保安全，他才能采取措施应对这一威胁。

sentences.en: And his worry must have been that, you know, Messalina and her toy boy have, might have suborned the Praetorians.
sentences.zh: 他当时一定在担心，麦萨利娜和她的面首可能已经收买收罗了近卫军。

sentences.en: I mean, in the event they haven't, which perhaps suggests that the story has been slightly overblown, but we'll come to that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上他们并没有这样做，这也许表明这个故事被稍微夸大了，但我们一会儿会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But anyway, Claudius is in a position to send the Praetorians out and suppress the coup, which they do.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，克劳狄乌斯有能力派近卫军出去镇压这场政变，他们也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: So all the various conspirators are arrested and executed.
sentences.zh: 于是所有各路阴谋者都被逮捕并处决了。

sentences.en: Messalina has vanished.
sentences.zh: 麦萨利娜却消失了。

sentences.en: It turns out that she's gone to find her mother, which is, you know, in her moment of crisis, she wants mummy.
sentences.zh: 原来她是去找她母亲了，也就是说，在危机时刻，她想找妈妈。

sentences.en: And they are kind of closeted together in one of their kind of beautiful gardens that all the aristocracy in Rome have.
sentences.zh: 她们俩躲藏在罗马所有贵族都有的那种美丽花园之一里。

sentences.en: And she's cornered there, run through by the Praetorians and dumped at the feet of her mother.
sentences.zh: 她在那里被逼入绝境，被近卫军长矛刺穿，并被扔在她母亲的脚边。

sentences.en: And that is the end of Messalina.
sentences.zh: 麦萨利娜的故事就此结束。

sentences.en: And so the question is, well, what, you know, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Now, I think it's evident from contemporaneous sources that Messalina is a very proficient player in power politics,
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为从同代人的资料中可以明显看出，麦萨利娜是权力政治中一个非常精明的玩家，

sentences.en: that she's very ruthless in getting rid of potential rivals or anyone who seems to threaten her position, that she's very ambitious, certainly, certainly ambitious for her son.
sentences.zh: 她为了除掉潜在的竞争对手或任何看似威胁她地位的人，手段极其冷酷无情，她非常有野心，当然，对她儿子更是野心勃勃。

sentences.en: And, I mean, maybe she's been cheating on Claudius.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，也许她一直背着克劳狄斯偷人。

sentences.en: Can't be sure.
sentences.zh: 无法确定。

sentences.en: But, you know, was she really conspiring against him?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，她真的在密谋反对他吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe people have, there's been a bit of an internal power struggle that we can't really glimpse and that maybe the bureaucrats,
sentences.zh: 对，也许人们曾有过，发生了一场我们无法真正窥见的内部权力斗争，也许那些官僚，

sentences.en: the freedmen have, you know, turned against her.
sentences.zh: 那些解放奴隶，你知道的，背叛了她。

sentences.en: Is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这可能吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 完全可能。

sentences.en: That concubine who goes to see Claudius at Ostia, she is prompted by one of Claudius's most powerful freedmen.
sentences.zh: 那个在奥斯提亚去见克劳狄斯的妃子，她是受克劳狄斯手下最有权势的一个解放奴隶指使的。

sentences.en: And they are lurking in the background of this whole episode.
sentences.zh: 他们潜伏在整个事件的背景中。

sentences.en: So it is, I think, likelier that Messalina is destroyed in a kind of faction fight between her supporters and kind of over-mighty freedmen
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，美索利娜更有可能是死于她的支持者与那些权势熏天的解放奴隶之间的一种派系斗争，

sentences.en: than that she really was kind of getting up to kind of all kinds of sexual shenanigans.
sentences.zh: 而不是她真的去搞了各种各样的性爱勾当。

sentences.en: So like the last days of Boris Johnson, where there was rival briefing between his wife, Carrie, and some of his aides, remember?
sentences.zh: 所以就像鲍里斯·约翰逊的最后日子，当时他的妻子凯瑞和一些助手之间存在敌对简报，还记得吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that kind of...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种……

sentences.en: I mean, I think from the point of view of Roman history, this is a key moment because, you know, this is a huge event.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为从罗马历史的角度来看，这是一个关键时刻，因为，你知道的，这是一件大事。

sentences.en: There are clearly all kinds of political interests at stake, but we just don't know what the truth is.
sentences.zh: 显然有各种各样的政治利益与之相关，但我们只是不知道真相是什么。

sentences.en: And it points to the way in which rivalries that for centuries and centuries have been played out on the floor of the Senate House
sentences.zh: 这表明，几个世纪以来一直在元老院议事大厅上演的权力争夺，

sentences.en: are now being conducted in side rooms and passageways and bedrooms in the Palatine.
sentences.zh: 现在正转移到帕拉蒂尼山的侧厅、走廊和卧室里进行。

sentences.en: And it means that certainty is impossible.
sentences.zh: 这意味着确定性是不可能的。

sentences.en: And the lack of certainty in turn breeds scandalous gossip.
sentences.zh: 而缺乏确定性反过来又孕育了丑闻般的流言蜚语。

sentences.en: And that's what explains these incredibly lurid stories.
sentences.zh: 这就是这些极其耸人听闻的故事的解释。

sentences.en: Again, I, Claudius, has great fun with these, that she has been, you know, you describe it in your notes as an all-day sex-a-thon.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，《我，克劳狄斯》在这方面玩得很开心，说她一直，你知道的，你在笔记中把它描述为一场全天的马拉松式性爱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: With Rome's top courtesan.
sentences.zh: 对象是罗马顶级的名妓。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Rome's most experienced and seasoned whore, and they go head-to-head, it is said, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以是罗马最有经验、最老道的妓女，据说她们可以说是针锋相对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Messalina wins.
sentences.zh: 而美索利娜赢了。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: That obviously didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 这显然没有发生。

sentences.en: No, it obviously didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 不，这显然没有发生。

sentences.en: And also what obviously didn't happen is what Juvenal claims in his poem.
sentences.zh: 而且显然也没有发生尤维纳利斯在他的诗中所声称的那种事。

sentences.en: So he's a satirist writing kind of maybe half a century or so after Messalina's death.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个讽刺作家，写作时间大概在美索利娜死后半个世纪左右。

sentences.en: And he describes her as kind of nostalgie de la boue, going off and working incognita in a low-rent brothel.
sentences.zh: 他把她描述为患有“爱泥癖”，隐姓埋名地去一家低档妓院做工。

sentences.en: And Juvenal says that she gilds her nipples and wears a blonde wig over her hair and kind of lies in this dirty, dirty room where plebeians come and have their way with her.
sentences.zh: 尤维纳利斯说，她给乳头镀金，头上戴着金色假发，躺在这个肮脏不堪的房间里，任由平民们进来对她胡作非为。

sentences.en: And this is clearly not true, but it suggests the kind of titillation that these faction fights in the Palatine are now capable of generating.
sentences.zh: 这显然不是真的，但它暗示了帕拉蒂尼山的这些派系斗争现在所能引发的那种香艳刺激感。

sentences.en: And of course, it's very bad for Messalina's posthumous reputation, but it's also terrible for Claudius's posthumous reputation.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对美索利娜身后的名声非常不利，但对克劳狄斯身后的名声也同样糟糕。

sentences.en: And in fact, his reputation when he's still alive, because it leaves him with a double problem.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当他还活着的时候名声就很差，因为这给他留下了一个双重问题。

sentences.en: It leaves him looking kind of weak, cook-holded, deluded.
sentences.zh: 这让他看起来软弱、被戴绿帽子、受蒙蔽。

sentences.en: And that plays into all the stories that are being told about him as the kind of the plaything of his freedman.
sentences.zh: 这迎合了所有关于他如何成为解放奴隶玩物的传言。

sentences.en: But it's also deprived him of a kind of crucial buttress upholding his regime, because he no longer has a marital link to the bloodline of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 但这剥夺了他维系政权的关键支柱，因为他不再拥有与奥古斯都血脉相连的婚姻纽带。

sentences.en: And he clearly feels that this is so important that he is prepared to offend some of the most sacred laws of Rome to deal with the problem,
sentences.zh: 他显然觉得这如此重要，以至于他准备冒犯罗马一些最神圣的法律来解决这个问题，

sentences.en: because there is a suitable candidate on hand.
sentences.zh: 因为手头正好有一个合适的人选。

sentences.en: There is a woman who, you know, she's not just a great-grandnie, she's a great-granddaughter of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 有这样一个女人，你知道的，她不仅是奥古斯都的曾侄女，她还是奥古斯都的曾孙女。

sentences.en: And this is one of the two surviving sisters of Caligula.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡利古拉两个在世的妹妹中的一个。

sentences.en: The pair of them, people may remember, had been exiled to a prison island by their brother.
sentences.zh: 大家可能还记得，这两人曾被她们的兄弟流放到一个监狱岛上。

sentences.en: And when Claudius came to power, he'd allowed them to return.
sentences.zh: 而当克劳狄斯掌权时，他允许她们回来了。

sentences.en: And he'd become very close to one of them, a woman called Agrippina.
sentences.zh: 并且他与其中一个名叫阿格里皮娜的女人变得非常亲密。

sentences.en: So like her mother, confusingly.
sentences.zh: 所以和她母亲的名字一样，这很让人混淆。

sentences.en: So she's called Agrippina the Younger by historians.
sentences.zh: 因此历史学家称她为小阿格里皮娜。

sentences.en: And she's very beautiful, very smart.
sentences.zh: 她非常美丽，非常聪明。

sentences.en: Claudius thinks she's great.
sentences.zh: 克劳狄斯认为她很棒。

sentences.en: But I think unless his need had been what it was, he would not have passed the law revoking the taboo against an uncle marrying his niece.
sentences.zh: 但我想，如果不是需求迫切，他是绝不会通过废除叔叔娶侄女禁忌的法律的。

sentences.en: And he says, no, this is absolutely legitimate.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，这完全是合法的。

sentences.en: And he goes ahead and he marries Agrippina.
sentences.zh: 于是他继续前进，娶了阿格里皮娜。

sentences.en: And Suetonius says, as he was getting ready to marry Agrippina in defiance of all morality,
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯说，当他准备迎娶阿格里皮娜以公然违背所有道德时，

sentences.en: he kept describing her in every speech he gave as his daughter, his ward, born and raised in his loving embrace.
sentences.zh: 他在每一次演讲中都不停地称她为他的女儿、他的受监护人，是在他慈爱的怀抱中出生和抚养长大的。

sentences.en: So it's very creepy.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: But more than that, it's evidence of his desperation still, even though he's now about a decade into his reign.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，这也证明了他依然感到绝望，尽管他的统治已经持续了大约十年。

sentences.en: The sense of insecurity, the anxiety that he's not a real Caesar and he needs a wife who will make him feel a real Caesar.
sentences.zh: 那种不安全感，那种担心自己不是真正的凯撒、需要一个妻子来让自己感觉自己是真正的凯撒的焦虑。

sentences.en: Just to give people a sense of it.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念。

sentences.en: He is 59.
sentences.zh: 他59岁。

sentences.en: She is 34.
sentences.zh: 她34岁。

sentences.en: So a 25 year, exactly 25 year age gap.
sentences.zh: 所以有25岁的差距，正好25岁的年龄差。

sentences.en: And she already has a son of her own who is much older than Britannicus, right?
sentences.zh: 而且她已经有了一个自己的儿子，比不列塔尼库斯大得多，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, four or five years older, which when you're 12, as Agrippina's son is, I mean, that's quite an age gap.
sentences.zh: 对，大四五岁，当你不列塔尼库斯那么大、12岁的时候，我是说，这可是相当大的年龄差。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this is a young lad called Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, after his father.
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫卢修斯·多米提乌斯·阿赫诺巴巴斯的年轻男孩，随他父亲的名字。
zh_words: 卢修斯·多米提乌斯·阿赫诺巴巴斯

sentences.en: And he, of course, has two advantages over Britannicus.
sentences.zh: 当然，他比不列塔尼库斯有两个优势。

sentences.en: So one of them we've just mentioned, the fact that he's older.
sentences.zh: 其中一个我们刚刚提到了，就是他年龄更大。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you're in your teens, being four or five years older is a considerable advantage.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你处于青少年时期，大四五岁是一个相当大的优势。

sentences.en: And the other thing, of course, is that he's a direct descendant of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个优势是他是奥古斯都的直系后代。

sentences.en: And there's a third advantage, which is that Agrippina is really, really ambitious to see him rather than Britannicus on the throne.
sentences.zh: 还有第三个优势，那就是阿格里皮娜非常非常渴望看到他而不是不列塔尼库斯登上皇位。

sentences.en: And she presses Claudius to adopt this young lad.
sentences.zh: 她敦促克劳狄斯收养这个年轻人。

sentences.en: And sure enough, on the 25th of February 50, so very shortly after his marriage to Agrippina, Claudius adopts the young Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，在公元50年2月25日，也就是他与阿格里皮娜结婚后不久，克劳狄斯收养了年轻的卢修斯·多米提乌斯·阿赫诺巴巴斯。
zh_words: 卢修斯·多米提乌斯·阿赫诺巴巴斯

sentences.en: And the boy formally becomes Claudius's eldest son.
sentences.zh: 这个男孩正式成为克劳狄斯的长子。

sentences.en: And as a marker of this, he takes on a new name.
sentences.zh: 作为标志，他起了一个新名字。

sentences.en: And this new name is Nero Claudius Caesar, or as we know him, Nero.
sentences.zh: 这个新名字叫尼禄·克劳狄斯·凯撒，或者按我们所知的叫尼禄。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this isn't going to end well.
sentences.zh: 所以这不会有好结果。

sentences.en: I mean, to be fair to Agrippina, she might well be thinking, if I don't do this,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，公平地说，阿格里皮娜很可能会想，如果我不这么做，

sentences.en: one day Britannicus will become emperor and he'll probably kill my son because my son will be a rival claimant.
sentences.zh: 总有一天不列塔尼库斯会成为皇帝，他很可能会杀了我儿子，因为我儿子将是一个潜在的竞争对手。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly what she thinks.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是她所想的。

sentences.en: And I think that even if the name of Nero didn't cast the shadow that it does, I think just listening to that set up, you know, it has the quality of a kind of folktale.
sentences.zh: 我想，即使“尼禄”这个名字没有带来现在这样的阴影，仅仅听听这个设定，你知道的，它就有一种民间故事的特质。

sentences.en: And you can see, you know, it's kind of Cinderella story, the befuddled father, you know, obsessing over a new wife, the child who gets abandoned.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出，你知道的，这有点像灰姑娘的故事，糊涂的父亲，你知道的，痴迷于新妻子，被抛弃的孩子。

sentences.en: All these kind of elements are there.
sentences.zh: 所有这些元素都在那里。

sentences.en: And sure enough, on 13th of October, 54, so Claudius has been powered by this point, just under 14 years, an announcement is released from the Palatine to the Roman people.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，在公元54年10月13日，此时克劳狄斯执政刚刚不到14年，帕拉蒂尼山向罗马人民发布了一则公告。

sentences.en: And this announcement says that Claudius is dead.
sentences.zh: 这则公告宣布克劳狄斯已死。

sentences.en: And shortly afterwards, Nero, who by this point is 16 years old, he comes out from the Palatine.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，此时已经16岁的尼禄从帕拉蒂尼山走了出来。

sentences.en: He's hailed by a Praetorian escort as Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他被近卫军护卫簇拥着欢呼为凯撒。

sentences.en: He's placed in a litter and as Claudius had been some 14 years previously, he is taken to the Praetorian camp.
sentences.zh: 他被抬进轿子里，就像14年前的克劳狄斯一样，被带到了近卫军军营。

sentences.en: So Agrippina and Nero likewise have recognized that this is the key to seizing power of the camp.
sentences.zh: 所以阿格里皮娜和尼禄同样认识到，这是夺取军营权力的关键。

sentences.en: Within a year, Britannicus is dead, supposedly of a seizure.
sentences.zh: 不到一年，不列塔尼库斯就死了，据说是死于中风。

sentences.en: But of course, everyone assumes that Nero has had him poisoned.
sentences.zh: 但当然，所有人都认为尼禄派人毒死了他。

sentences.en: And Agrippina herself dies in 59.
sentences.zh: 阿格里皮娜本人则在59年去世。

sentences.en: She is definitely murdered by Nero.
sentences.zh: 她绝对是被尼禄谋杀的。

sentences.en: I mean, Nero makes no bones about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，尼禄对此毫不掩饰。

sentences.en: And Nero himself, of course, dies in 68.
sentences.zh: 当然，尼禄本人也在68年去世。

sentences.en: As we heard in the, you know, the details of how he died, we heard in the very opening reading of this series.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在本系列开篇朗读中所听到的，关于他如何死去的细节。

sentences.en: And with him dies Augustus's bloodline.
sentences.zh: 随着他的死去，奥古斯都的血脉断绝了。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: There are no more heirs of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 再也没有奥古斯都的继承人了。

sentences.en: Let's go back to Claudius for a second.
sentences.zh: 让我们再回到克劳狄斯。

sentences.en: He died in October 54.
sentences.zh: 他在54年10月去世。

sentences.en: So that's what, four years after he'd adopted Nero as his heir.
sentences.zh: 所以那是，在他收养尼禄为继承人四年后。

sentences.en: And it's always thought, isn't it, thanks largely probably to Suetonius and also to I, Claudius, that he was poisoned by Agrippina and Nero with mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 人们一直认为，对吧，这很大程度上要归功于苏埃托尼乌斯以及《我，克劳狄斯》，认为他和蘑菇一起被阿格里皮娜和尼禄毒死了。

sentences.en: Suetonius says he was poisoned with a dish of mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯说他是被一盘蘑菇毒死的。

sentences.en: Do you think that's true?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, so I think when Suetonius is the first to report something,
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我想，当苏埃托尼乌斯是第一个报道某件事的人时，

sentences.en: that's when you need to be on your guard.
sentences.zh: 那就是你需要保持警惕的时候。

sentences.en: That's suspicious.
sentences.zh: 这很可疑。

sentences.en: Suetonius is not the first to report that Claudius was murdered by, with a dish of poisoned mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯并不是第一个报道克劳狄斯是被一盘毒蘑菇谋杀的人。

sentences.en: So Pliny the Elder mentions it.
sentences.zh: 老普林尼提到了这一点。

sentences.en: But, I mean, having said that, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 但是，话虽如此，我们并不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe he dies of natural causes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许他是自然死亡。

sentences.en: I mean, he'd been sickly all his life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他一生体弱多病。

sentences.en: He's had a good innings.
sentences.zh: 他已经活得很久了。

sentences.en: You know, he's 63 when he finally pops his clogs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他63岁时终于一命呜呼。

sentences.en: And there's Gisar Alsgood.
sentences.zh: 还有吉萨·阿尔斯古德。

sentences.en: He's written a brilliant book on Claudius, Claudius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本关于克劳狄斯的杰出著作，《克劳狄斯·凯撒》。

sentences.en: In that, he points out that there had been a lot of plague in Rome at the time.
sentences.zh: 在书中，他指出当时罗马曾发生过很多瘟疫。

sentences.en: He points to evidence from Tacitus of people, a large number of high-ranking people who died.
sentences.zh: 他指出了塔西佗关于人们的证据，大量高层人士死亡。

sentences.en: So that suggests that there's quite a lot of sickness around.
sentences.zh: 这表明当时周围有很多疾病。

sentences.en: And the honest truth is, is that we can't know.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我们无法得知真相。

sentences.en: And I guess that, I mean, you would say as a historian who has, you know, I mean, think of all the episodes we did on 1968 or Kennedy or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我想，作为一个历史学家，你会说，你知道的，想想我们做过的所有关于1968年或肯尼迪之类的节目。

sentences.en: I mean, there's so much material that this is a cause of frustration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有这么多的材料，这真是一个令人沮丧的原因。

sentences.en: But I think it's also, it breeds what, to me, is part of the fascination of this period
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，这孕育了我所认为的这段时期的一部分魅力，

sentences.en: and of Suetonius' biographies, which is the way that recorded fact and myth kind of blur into one another.
sentences.zh: 以及苏埃托尼乌斯传记的魅力，那就是有据可查的事实和神话相互交织在一起的方式。

sentences.en: And sometimes you can distinguish the lineaments of history, and other times you see the lineaments of mythology.
sentences.zh: 有时你能辨认出历史的轮廓，有时你又会看到神话的轮廓。

sentences.en: And trying to make sense of that, for me, is what makes this whole story so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，试图理解这一点正是让整个故事如此引人入胜的原因。

sentences.en: You know, we talked about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们讨论过。

sentences.en: This is the ultimate dynastic story.
sentences.zh: 这是终极的王朝故事。

sentences.en: It's why Claudius,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么克劳狄斯，

sentences.en: you know, as a novel, but even more as a TV drama, kind of lies at the head of all these great dynastic epics that we've had on TV over the past decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为一部小说，甚至更作为一部电视剧，在过去几十年里，它位居我们看过的所有这些伟大王朝史诗之首。

sentences.en: And the fact that Suetonius' account has this kind of mythic folkloric quality, as well as kind of quoting letters and, you know, citing laws and things,
sentences.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯的叙述具有这种神话般的民间传说特质，同时又引用书信、法律等内容，

sentences.en: I think is a crucial part of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是其中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: No, I'd agree.
sentences.zh: 不，我同意。

sentences.en: I agree completely.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意。

sentences.en: But actually, where I'd slightly probably disagree with you, is I don't necessarily think this is actually as different from modern history as you would think.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我可能稍微不同意你的一点是，我不认为这真的与你想象的现代历史有那么大不同。

sentences.en: So modern history, too, is freighted with all kinds of assumptions, folk myths, urban myths.
sentences.zh: 所以现代历史也充斥着各种各样的假设、民间神话、都市神话。

sentences.en: And actually teasing out what really happened is the impossible goal for any historian of any period.
sentences.zh: 事实上，理清到底发生了什么对于任何时期的任何历史学家来说都是一个不可能实现的目标。

sentences.en: I was just thinking about the, you know, when I was thinking about the death of Claudius and, you know, was he murdered, was he not?
sentences.zh: 我刚才在想，你知道的，当我思考克劳狄斯的死时，他是被谋杀的，还是没有？

sentences.en: And then, of course, thinking about that series we did on Kennedy and kind of yearning for the equivalent of a Warren report or something.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，想到了我们制作的关于肯尼迪的那个系列，并渴望有一份沃伦报告之类的东西来替代。

sentences.en: You know, all the kind of the whole range of pieces of evidence that you could bring to bear and thinking how frustrating it is we don't have that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有你可以提出的各种证据，然后一想到我们没有这些是多么令人沮丧。

sentences.en: But, of course, Kennedy is a myth, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，肯尼迪是一个神话，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And also, which wouldn't solve the, you know, wouldn't end the conversation.
sentences.zh: 而且，这也无法解决，你知道的，无法结束对话。

sentences.en: I mean, because these things don't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为这些事情是不会结束的。

sentences.en: So if people want to make up their own minds, what they should do is to buy Tom's new translation
sentences.zh: 所以，如果人们想自己做决定，他们应该做的是去买汤姆的新译本，

sentences.en: of Suetonius' book, The Lives of the Caesars, which is available now from all good bookshops with Penguin Classics.
sentences.zh: 即苏埃托尼乌斯的书《恺撒传》，企鹅经典丛书，各大优秀书店现已发售。

sentences.en: Tom, a great translation, a great series, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这真是一个伟大的翻译，一部伟大的系列，我必须得说。

sentences.en: A tour de force, I think, is the approved Restless History terminology.
sentences.zh: 我想，按照《动荡历史》的惯用术语，这堪称一部代表作。

sentences.en: So that was absolutely tremendous.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是太棒了。

sentences.en: And by the way, the book is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这本书非常精彩。

sentences.en: So people should absolutely go and buy the book.
sentences.zh: 所以大家一定要去买这本书。

sentences.en: And we will be back next week with something very different, another of History's Great Monsters, actually, and another story in which it's actually quite difficult to get at,
sentences.zh: 我们下周将带着完全不同的内容回归，实际上是另一个“历史上的伟大恶魔”，而且是另一个故事，在这个故事中，

sentences.en: as it were, the truth of what really happened, because there are so many different accounts.
sentences.zh: 要想弄清真正发生的事情的真相其实相当困难，因为有太多不同的说法。

sentences.en: And that is the story of King Leopold and the Belgian Congo.
sentences.zh: 这就是利奥波德国王和比利时刚果的故事。

sentences.en: So we will be telling that story next week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们下周将讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: The Heart of Darkness, indeed.
sentences.zh: 的确，这就是黑暗之心。

sentences.en: OK, on that bombshell, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 好了，带着这个惊人的消息，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
